question: In a triangle ABC, D and E are points on BC such that AD = AE and ∠BAD = ∠CAE. If AB = (2p + 3), BD = 2p, AC = (3q - 1) and CE = q, then find the value of (p + q).
solution:
**Given:**

D = AE and ∠BAD = ∠CAE

AB = (2p + 3), BD = 2p, AC = (3q - 1) and CE = q

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b7f8cfe8c179f9fa4e0e37384e635f722930c33db3533e38204d48c4276aab5b.png] 

In ΔABD and ΔAEC,

AD = AE [Given]

∠ADB = ∠AEC [Exterior angles of ΔADE, where ∠ADE = ∠AED]

∠BAD = ∠CAE [Given]

So, ΔADB ∼ ΔAEC [A - S - A rule]

Then, 

⇒ AB/AC = BD/CE = AD/AE

⇒ (2p + 3)/(3q - 1) = 2p/q = 1 [∵ AD = AE]

By taking 2p/q = 1 

⇒ 2p = q .....(1)

By taking (2p + 3)/(3q - 1) = 1 

⇒ 2p + 3 = 3q - 1

⇒ 3q - 2p = 3 + 1

⇒ 3q - q = 4 [∵ 2p = q]

⇒ 2q = 4

⇒ q = 4/2 = 2

Put q = 2 in equation (1),

2p = 2

⇒ p = 2/2 = 1

Then, (p + q) = 1 + 2 = 3

**∴ The value of (p + q) is 3**
